newsitem.title: ITALY: Berlusconi ally to stand trial on Mafia charges.
newsitem.headline: Berlusconi ally to stand trial on Mafia charges.

text.p: Marcello dell'Utri, former chairman of Italian media mogul Silvio Berlusconi's advertising firm Publitalia, was on Friday ordered by a Sicilian judge to stand trial on charges of mafia association.

Dell'Utri, a parliamentary deputy for centre-right opposition leader Berlusconi's Forza Italia party, is already on trial in Milan and Turin on charges of false billing, false accounting and tax fraud while at Publitalia.
The Palermo trial will start on October 15.

The Sicilian-born Dell'Utri, who met anti-Mafia investigators several times last year to answer questions, was ordered to stand trial after allegations against him by mob turncoats who said that he had informal ties with the Mafia.

They have reportedly claimed that Dell'Utri's ties with the Mafia began in the 1960s as an occasional point of contact between the Mafia, Milanese business circles and institutional authorities, and continued until 1995.
Dell'Utri resigned from his job at Publitalia, part of Berlusconi's Fininvest empire, in 1995 when the false billing charges against him emerged.
Former Prime Minister Berlusconi defended him last year by saying he could more easily imagine his former business colleague as a Martian than a Mafioso.
